claim: A 22-second dance video becomes a Unitree G1 reference motion on one 24 GB RTX 3090 Ti in about 7 minutes through retarget_video (GEM-X 372 to 407 s at 6.5 GB peak on the card, the SOMA Retargeter 19 s), and mjlab's tracking task learns from such references only with many worlds: one world learned nothing in 600 iterations, 4,096 worlds tracked NVIDIA's mocap walk for 425 of its 453 steps after 500 iterations (1.9 s each, 4.2 GB), and the court dance from video rose from 8 to 39 steps over the same 500.
instrument: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3090 Ti, 24,564 MiB, driver 610.88, PCIe 4.0 x8, WSL2 (Linux 6.18.58.1-microsoft-standard-WSL2), 31 GB of RAM in the VM, the Studio open (about 2.4 GB of the card before each run); GEM-X 4aef145 (torch 2.11.0+cu128, py-soma-x 0.3.3) and the SOMA Retargeter cbdb2b4 (warp 1.16.0, newton 1.3.0) each in its own uv env; mjlab as pinned in trainnr-mjlab's lock

inputs.footage: court-dance: Mixkit 51314 'Talented urban woman dancing at night on a basketball court', 1280x720 H.264, 23.976 fps, 21.938 s (Mixkit Stock Video Free License), the clip GEM-X's own demo credits
inputs.gem_x_weights: nvidia/GEM-X @ b111f2dcf3ebcf57965fd53499cb645dfa5ba25c: body_s240000.ckpt, vitpose.pth, motion_native77_e774_s292175.ckpt, body_video_native77.yaml; nvidia/SOMA-X v0.3.3; YOLOX-X HumanArt sha256 8e9ea96a176bd48501eaaa77216e49ee30794d2f8ba80c7b9862beca4ea972da
inputs.control_motion: the SOMA Retargeter's sample Neutral_walk_forward_002__A057.bvh (NVIDIA Sample Data Evaluation License; 1,103 frames at 120 fps), retargeted to the G1 the same way

runs.name: court-dance-g1
runs.note: stage times from the job log

retarget_video.retarget_note: the same retarget took 35 s on the CPU and 105 s on the GPU when run by hand (warp chose by whether it found the CUDA driver); the job's 19 s ran on the GPU

floor.note: GEM-X's world floor leaned 12.8 degrees: over 22 s the hips rose 70 cm; a plane fitted to each frame's lowest foot, turned level, and a 1 s floor under the feet bring the hips to a dancer's range

one_world.note: mjlab's scripts/train.py trains one world unless --env.scene.num-envs is given; the NVIDIA walk did not learn (the dance alike over 600 iterations, reward -1.35 to -1.84)

dance_4096.note: the smoothed court-dance reference; learning, more slowly than the walk

artifacts.recordings/court-dance-g1: the reference retarget_video wrote in the g1-dance test project: recording.json, signals.npz, raw/ (gem-x.pt, soma.bvh, retargeted.csv, motion.npz, replay.mp4)
artifacts.recordings/court-dance-g1-live: the second run, with its live stream kept as raw/stream.rrd

protocol: Each retarget_video run is one trainnr job from the footage folder: GEM-X motion-video with --postprocess, gem_to_bvh (level floor), the SOMA Retargeter's batch converter onto unitree_g1, the 6 Hz smoothing, mjlab's MotionLoader replay at 50 fps, a kinematic replay video. GPU memory sampled every 0.5 s by nvidia-smi. Tracking runs: mjlab's Mjlab-Tracking-Flat-Unitree-G1 config, logger tensorboard, WANDB_MODE disabled; episode length and reward read from rsl_rl's console, averaged over the iteration windows named.
caveats: One clip, one machine: GEM-X's time scales with the clip and its memory was not searched for a ceiling.
The tracking numbers are 500 iterations; mjlab's tracking config allows 30,000. Whether the dance is tracked to its end is not measured yet, nor any evaluation with an interval.
The floor levelling assumes one foot near the floor most of the time; a clip of jumps or a person lying down needs another rule.
The reference is kinematic: it was never on a robot, and its basis is unknown.
